items.name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
ingredients: 8 ounces (225 grams) dried spaghetti, or any pasta you have around
4 tablespoons (60 ml) olive oil, plus more to finish
4 cloves garlic, minced, or whatever amount feels right
¼ to ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes and/or many grinds of black pepper
A big handful of chopped flat-leaf parsley
steps: In well-salted water, boil your spaghetti until it’s 1 to 2 minutes shy of done. Before draining it, set aside 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the rest. In your empty pan, combine olive oil, garlic, and pepper flakes and then turn the heat to medium.
[Starting the mixture cold is how I keep the garlic from cooking too fast.] Cook, stirring, until the garlic begins to take on a golden color.

Add the drained pasta and half the reserved cooking water and heat together, stirring vigorously, until the pasta water and garlic oil combine to make a glossy coating for the spaghetti. Add more of the reserved pasta water as needed to keep it loose — I almost always use the second half-cup.
Toss in parsley, any additional seasoning, if needed, and serve right away with an extra drizzle of olive oil on top. Parmesan on top is not traditional, but your house, your rules, okay?

items.name: Marry Me Chicken
ingredients: 1 ½ lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
½ cup julienned sun-dried tomatoes chopped
steps: Season chicken with 1 teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper.

Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Working in batches, add chicken to the Dutch oven in a single layer and cook until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 4-5 minutes per side; set aside.
Stir in tomato paste, garlic, oregano, thyme and red pepper flakes until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Whisk in flour until lightly browned, about 1 minute.
Stir in wine, scraping any browned bits from the bottom of the Dutch oven.
Stir in chicken stock, heavy cream and sun-dried tomatoes; season with salt and pepper, to taste.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened and flavors have blended, about 5 minutes. If the mixture is too thick, add more stock as needed.
Stir in Parmesan and basil. Return chicken to the Dutch oven.
Serve warm.

items.name: House Lemonade
ingredients: 1 cup (235 ml) fresh lemon juice (from 5-6 lemons)
2 cups (475 ml) cold water, plus up to 1 more
steps: Pour the lemon juice through a sieve to remove pulp, then into a pitcher. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Add the first two cups of cold water. This is the lemonade base I use. It keeps in the fridge for several days, but tastes best on the first two.
→ To make a finished pitcher of lemonade, add ice, and ½ to 1 cup more cold water to taste.
→ To make a glass of fizzy lemonade, pour it over ice until ⅔ to ¾ of the way up the glass and finish with seltzer.

For other flavors: You could swap one of the cups of water with watermelon juice, or ½ cup with strained raspberry or blackberry purée, or, as I did for friends this week, swap the sugar with maple syrup and shake it up with some mint leaves and bourbon.

items.name: Hot Dogs with Vinegared Iceberg and Potato Chips
ingredients: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (Diamond brand; use half of any other)
Half a small head of iceberg, cut into ¼-inch ribbons (about 2 cups)
steps: Prepare the vinegared iceberg: Stir water, vinegar, salt, and sugar in a bowl until salt and sugar dissolve. Add iceberg and toss to coat. Transfer to the fridge for as little as 30 minutes and up to 1 day.

Cook your hot dogs: Split each of your hot dogs down the center, but leave the bottom hinge intact. Open and place cut side-down on a grill or in a griddle pan on the stove. [I’m using these presses as a weight for extra browning.

] Hot dogs are already fully cooked from the package so you’re cooking until you get the sizzle, color, and browned crisp that you want. For extra crisp, you can flip the butterflied hot dogs over and cook on the skin side too.

Assemble: Fold each hot dog back together and arrange split side up in a bun. Add ketchup and mustard. Use tongs to grab some of the vinegared iceberg, shaking off the extra liquid, and pile on top. Top with white onion, crumbled chips, and freshly ground black pepper. Eat right away. Make more as soon as possible.
